h1:
Hua Hin Food Guide
Seafood, Night Markets, Cafes & Souvenirs
intro: Hua Hin is a seaside town close to Bangkok where you can eat all day without repeating yourself — fresh seafood right by the beach, a night market in the town center after dark, and sea-view cafes around Khao Takiab. We've picked spots and neighborhoods that are genuinely open, with rough prices, so you can plan your meals before you even set off.

blocks.html: What makes eating in Hua Hin fun is the variety packed into a short walk. The town center has the night market and some long-running seafood restaurants, while the Khao Takiab–Nong Kae stretch is the cafe-and-seafood-by-the-water zone where you can linger from afternoon into the evening. This guide is split into seafood, night markets, cafes, and souvenirs, then closes with a short two-day eating plan you can follow straight off the page.

Seafood is the main reason people drive down to Hua Hin. The restaurants spread across three zones: the town center near the night market, the Khao Takiab beachfront, and the Nong Kae area. Dishes you'll see most often and that everyone orders include steamed blue crab, grilled prawns, scallops baked with butter, sea bass fried with fish sauce, and seafood tom yum. Prices depend on the day and the size of the seafood you pick.

items.name: Krua Lung Ja Seafood (Night Market)
items.blurb: A seafood spot inside the Hua Hin night market that draws plenty of Thai and foreign visitors. The standouts are scallops baked with garlic butter, crab stir-fried with curry powder, and grilled prawns. Open only from early evening into the late hours.

items.name: Jay Khiao Seafood
items.blurb: A long-standing seafood place in central Hua Hin, known for squid, crab, and tom yum. Prices are easy on the wallet for the portions, so it's great for a group sharing several dishes.

items.name: Saen Suk Som Seafood
items.blurb: A spot right on Takiab Beach, famous for crab fried rice and tom yum. You can sit and catch the sea breeze in a relaxed setting — good for lunch through the early evening.

items.name: Ao Takiab Seafood
items.blurb: A spot in the Khao Takiab–Hua Don beach zone, known for crab fried rice packed with meat and for mussels. Prices are friendly, and it's an easy stop after visiting Khao Takiab.

items.name: Koti
items.blurb: An old-school place in central Hua Hin that locals know well, known for dried squid, crab with chili dip, and curries. Prices aren't steep and the setting is classically simple.

items.name: Pa Ruay Pu Pen
items.blurb: In the Khao Takiab zone, the draw is live, fresh blue crab you pick yourself — steamed or stir-fried, your call. Prices are reasonable given how fresh it is.
items.meta: Khao Takiab · fresh crab focus · reasonable prices

items.name: Aroy@Hua Hin (Nong Kae)
items.blurb: A spot in the Nong Kae area, with prawn and crab tom yum as the standouts — bold and full-flavored. Prices are friendly, and it's handy if you're staying in the Nong Kae–Khao Takiab zone.

items.name: Baan Isara Seafood
items.blurb: A beachfront spot known for sea bass with fish sauce and seafood curry. You can sit to the sound of the waves — a nice setting in the evening, mid-range prices.

blocks.title: How to order without overpaying
blocks.html: Most seafood is priced by weight and size. Ask for the price per kilo and have it weighed in front of you before cooking — that's the safe way. Over long weekends and the late-to-early-year high season, seafood prices climb and the popular spots get long lines, so leave a little buffer for the wait.

blocks.html: Come evening, Hua Hin has several markets to graze through, each with its own mood — from the seafood-leaning downtown night market to the arty market set in a garden out by Khao Takiab. You can wander and snack your way through both savory bites and sweets.

items: Hua Hin Night Market (Dechanuchit Road) — the night market in the town center, open roughly 17:00 to midnight daily. It's strong on grilled seafood, grilled squid, grilled prawns, and crab stir-fried with curry powder, plus sweets like khanom buang and mango sticky rice. Come around 18:00–19:00 and every stall is open but it isn't yet packed.

Cicada Market, Khao Takiab — an arts market in a garden, open Friday to Sunday, roughly 16:30–23:00. There's a live music stage, photo corners, and a wide range of food and dessert stalls. It's easier to walk than the downtown night market and suits families and anyone after a chill evening.

Sam Phan Nam Floating Market — a retro-themed floating market with local eats, Thai sweets, and photo corners. Worth a stop in the afternoon to early evening if you want a different mood from the night markets.
Chatchai Market (morning market) — an old fresh market in the town center, ideal for early risers. There's rice-and-curry, old-style coffee, and fresh produce to browse — a local way to do breakfast.

blocks.title: An honest note on the markets
blocks.html: Cicada Market only opens Friday to Sunday — come on a weekday and it's closed, so check the day before you plan around it. The downtown night market gets very crowded over long weekends and parking is hard to find; better to park on the outer edges and walk in.

blocks.text: Hua Hin Cafes and Sea-View Coffee Spots

blocks.html: Hua Hin is a real cafe town. The standout zone is Khao Takiab–Nong Kae, where sea-view spots line up one after another and you can sip coffee in the breeze all afternoon. Many have both a beachfront area and an indoor space — good for photos and for resting after a day out. Most drinks run around ฿80–160.

items.name: Khao Takiab sea-view cafes
items.blurb: The Khao Takiab zone has several cafes right on the water where you can sit by the beach with views of the headland — best from late afternoon to sunset.

items.name: Beachfront resort cafes
items.blurb: Many resorts open their cafes to outside guests — calm settings with full drink and bakery menus, good for getting work done or settling in for a long while.

items.name: Downtown Hua Hin cafes
items.blurb: The town center has stylishly designed cafes within walking distance of each other — easy to drop into while shopping or before heading to the night market in the evening.

blocks.text: Souvenirs to Bring Home from Hua Hin

blocks.html: Before you head back, the popular Hua Hin souvenirs lean toward processed seafood and Thai sweets. You'll find them around Chatchai Market, the night market, and the souvenir shops along Phetkasem Road.

items: Dried seafood — dried squid, dried shrimp, salted fish, found at fresh markets and souvenir shops. Pick pieces that are fully dry and don't smell too sharp.
Khanom mo kaeng and Thai sweets — the Phetchaburi area next to Hua Hin is famous for khanom mo kaeng (Thai custard) and thong yip/thong yot. You can buy them on the way down or in Hua Hin town.
Shrimp paste, fish sauce, chili paste — souvenirs for the home cook. Choose tightly sealed packaging that's easy to carry — the kind of gift people actually use.
Seasonal fruit and fresh produce — in fruit season there's pineapple and coconut to choose from. If you're carrying it a long way home, go for fruit that isn't too ripe yet.

faq.q: What food should you try in Hua Hin?
faq.a: Seafood is the town's headline act — especially steamed blue crab, grilled prawns, scallops baked with butter, sea bass fried with fish sauce, and seafood tom yum. After that come the night-market bites like grilled squid, and sweets like khanom buang and mango sticky rice.

faq.q: Where should you eat seafood in Hua Hin, and roughly how much does it cost?
faq.a: In the town center, Jay Khiao and Koti are budget-friendly. Out on Khao Takiab beach, Saen Suk Som and Ao Takiab come with sea views. Prices are mostly based on the weight and size of the seafood, so ask for the price per kilo and have it weighed in front of you before cooking. Prices climb over long weekends.

faq.q: What time does the Hua Hin night market open?
faq.a: The Hua Hin night market on Dechanuchit Road opens around 17:00 to midnight daily. The window when all the stalls are open but it isn't yet packed is roughly 18:00–19:00. Cicada Market at Khao Takiab opens only Friday to Sunday, roughly 16:30–23:00.

faq.q: Which areas of Hua Hin have sea-view cafes?
faq.a: The zones with the most sea-view cafes lined up are Khao Takiab and Nong Kae. Many have both a beachfront area and an indoor space, with most drinks around 80–160 THB. Good for settling in from the afternoon into the evening.

faq.q: What souvenirs should you buy in Hua Hin?
faq.a: Processed seafood like dried squid, dried shrimp, and salted fish are popular souvenirs, along with Thai sweets and khanom mo kaeng from the neighboring Phetchaburi area. You'll find them around Chatchai Market, the night market, and the souvenir shops along Phetkasem Road.
